newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on corn, soybean rally.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on corn, soybean rally.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on rallies in the corn and soybean pits, traders said.
"It's all coming out of corn and beans," a trader said referring to the late gains in wheat futures.
Weather concerns and fund buying boosted the corn and soybean markets to sharply higher closes.

Some independent strength in wheat may have come from the export sector with Pakistan a buyer of U.S. wheat and European traders Tuesday said Jordan was expected in the market during August for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.
"The Pakistan wheat sale isn't necessarily supportive. But if it hadn't happened it would have been negative, it removes another unknown from the market," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Pakistan bought 500,000 tonnes of white wheat -- 200,000 from the U.S., 250,000 from Australia and 50,000 from Canada, according to the Pakistani embassy in Washington D.C.
CBOT soft red winter wheat closed 1/2 to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with September up 1/2 at $3.58 a bushel. December closed 3-1/2 higher at $3.74.

However, wheat gains were curbed by signals the market was technically overbought for the short term plus the U.S. has nearly completed harvest of an ample winter wheat crop that was virtually free of diseases.
The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the September closed at nearly 63 percent. An RSI of 70 or more is considered near overbought status for short term traders.

Mild underpinning may have come from a slight decline in the condition rating of the U.S. spring wheat crop. USDA Monday said the spring wheat crop as of Sunday was 50 percent good to excellent, below the 52 percent in that category the previous week.
Also USDA Monday said the U.S. winter wheat harvest was 79 percent complete as of Sunday, above the 78 percent a year ago and above the 77 percent average pace.
Persistent drier-than-desired weather in some Australia wheat growing areas and mounting concern about dry weather in China's grain/soy belt also helped underpin wheat futures, traders said.
Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of September and sold one million December, traders said. Term Commodities bought one million bushels of December.
Also, FIMAT Futures bought two million bushels of September, Tenco Inc bought 2.3 million bushels of December and Refco Inc sold 2.5 million bushels of December, floor sources said.

In spread dealings, Prudential Securities did 300,000 bushels of September/March at 22-1/2 cents, premium March and spread 200,000 bushels of December/March at nine cents, premium March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 18,000 contracts, below the 18,649 traded Monday.

In wheat options, Lee B. Stern and Co sold 500 September $3.70 calls at six cents, Refco Inc sold 200 March $3.30 puts at 8-1/2 cents and SAK Futures bought 200 December $3.80 calls at 18-1/2 to 19 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,500 contracts, above the 7,225 traded Monday.
